issues.legal_issue: Expiry of the period specified for a peace bond does not by itself make preventive peace proceedings nugatory while the apprehended danger continues.
material_facts: Proceedings were initiated over an alleged incident in 1959, and the appellants were ordered to furnish peace bonds for one year.
The bonds were not furnished because court orders stayed their execution, and the proceedings remained pending for years.
issues.conclusion: The proceedings could continue after the bond period expired if the apprehension of a breach of peace or disturbance of public tranquillity still persisted.
issues.legal_principle: Section 107 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, is preventive rather than penal and enables measures to prevent breaches of peace or disturbances of public tranquillity. Expiry of the bond period does not automatically terminate proceedings, since that would allow a person to defeat them by prolonging the case while the danger persists.

predicates.peacekeeping_proceeding: A proceeding was brought to prevent a person from causing a breach of peace or disturbing public tranquillity.
predicates.bond_term_expired: The period for which a person was ordered to furnish a peace bond had passed.
predicates.danger_of_breach_persists: The apprehension of a breach of peace or disturbance of public tranquillity continued.

issues.definition: When a peacekeeping proceeding concerns a danger that continues, expiry of the bond period does not prevent the proceeding from continuing.

issues.legal_issue: A prolonged period without untoward conduct may show that the danger underlying preventive peace proceedings has vanished, making it appropriate to discharge the person rather than require a peace bond.
material_facts: The proceedings arose from an incident in 1959 and remained pending for about thirteen years.
The appellants did not furnish the bonds because their execution had been stayed by the courts.
There was nothing to show that the appellants had done anything during that period that could cause an apprehension of a breach of peace.
issues.conclusion: In light of the long period without conduct giving rise to apprehension of a breach of peace, it was not expedient or essential to compel the appellants to furnish bonds, and they were discharged.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 107 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, the court may consider subsequent events and drop the proceedings and discharge the person if the danger has disappeared. Even without positive evidence of reconciliation, a very long period since the incident during which nothing untoward has happened may support an inference that the danger of a breach of peace has vanished. Because the proceeding affects the liberty of a person not found guilty of an offence, the preventive power must be exercised strictly in accordance with law.

predicates.peacekeeping_proceeding: A proceeding was brought to prevent a person from causing a breach of peace or disturbing public tranquillity.
predicates.long_time_elapsed: A very long period passed after the incident underlying the proceeding.
predicates.no_untoward_conduct: The person did nothing during that period that could give rise to an apprehension of a breach of peace.

issues.definition: When a peacekeeping proceeding remains pending for a very long time and the person has done nothing untoward during that time, the person may be discharged.
